title: Definition
observedConcepts: Integration of mechanical, electrical, software components; reprogrammability; tasks with and without human intervention.
Robotics studies design, programming and control.
Robot word: Slavic worker/compulsory work/drudgery; Karel Čapek R.U.R. 1920.
notes: Text fully readable; bottom-right empty rectangle contains no content.

title: First Robot
observedConcepts: Course states first commercial robot introduced 1962; Unimation USA, Engelberger with Devol, General Motors installation.
Unimate photo and schematic label rotary, radial, vertical, wrist bend, wrist yaw and wrist swivel motions.
notes: Historical date is a course claim; any question should explicitly attribute to this slide. Diagram small labels were legible but should use an enlarged crop for a figure question.

title: Types of Robots
observedConcepts: Manipulation main goal is action on environment.
notes: Two contrastive text groups, no quantitative diagram.

title: Mobile Robot Examples
observedConcepts: Wheeled robots for flat surfaces; Robotino example.
Walking/running robots have one or more legs and handle uneven terrain; BigDog example.
notes: Photographs and labels support class-example correspondence; flat/uneven not absolute physical impossibility claims.

title: Manipulator Examples
observedConcepts: Industrial robots teleoperated and autonomous; KUKA-KR5 named example.
notes: KUKA robot photo and hand/prosthesis pictures; no additional numerical labels.

title: Other Classification of Robots
observedConcepts: Fixed/mobile; serial/parallel; DOF; rigid/flexible; control point-to-point/autonomy/intelligence.
Older industrial robots fixed base, links connected by actuated joints.
Modern robots may move on factory floors/uneven terrain or walk/swim/fly.
notes: Each bullet is independent coverage, not collapsed to one taxonomy question.

title: Serial or parallel
observedConcepts: Serial chain fixed base, sequential links/joints, terminates in end-effector.
Slide describes parallel robot as more than one loop and no natural end-effector.
PUMA560 diagram labels waist/shoulder/forearm and three wrist rotations.
Parallel-platform diagram labels top platform, spherical joint, prismatic joint, U joint, extensible leg, fixed base and actuator motion.
notes: No natural end-effector is slide-specific phrasing, not universal definition. Diagram labels readable. Source statement must not imply parallel robots cannot carry tools.

title: Degree-of-Freedom (DOF)
observedConcepts: Course connects capability and actuated joints to DOF.
Six DOF for arbitrary 3D task; painting/welding five; electronics assembly four-DOF SCARA.
Mounting 5/6-DOF robot on 2/3-DOF gantry or mobile robot adds flexibility/working volume.
More than six DOF redundancy helps obstacle avoidance/flexibility.
notes: Examples refer to this course setting; avoid claiming six DOF guarantees reachability or every actuated joint always supplies independent motion.

title: Joint arrangement classification
observedConcepts: First three joints classify fixed serial robots: Cartesian/spherical/cylindrical and anthropomorphic human-arm-like.
SCARA expanded here as Selective Compliance Adaptive Robot Arm; electronic assembly.
Last three joints form wrist and orient end-effector.
notes: No title at top. Use course wording for SCARA expansion; keep positioning/orientation roles distinct.

title: Rigid Vs. Flexible
observedConcepts: Heavy rigid industrial robots for required accuracy.
Weight minimization in space leads to flexible links/joints.
notes: Industrial manipulator photo contrasted with space-arm photo. Images add setting, no extra quantitative claims.

title: Control and Mode of Operation
observedConcepts: Teach/playback manual demonstration records positions and repeats taught sequence; time-consuming, cannot react to environmental changes as described.
Computer controlled inputs often tried offline.
Sensor-driven avoids obstacles and makes decisions.
Intelligent robots learn about environment using AI.
notes: All four modes and limitations independently examinable; intelligent is not equivalent to mere stored playback.

title: Asimov's 3 Laws of Robotics
observedConcepts: First never harm humans; second obey humans subject to first; third protect self subject to other laws.
Priority is human safety then permitted obedience then self-preservation.
notes: Fictional laws attributed to 1940s short story; do not imply legal requirements. Three enumerated rules visually clear.

title: The Mechanics & Control of Mechanical Manipulators
observedConcepts: Body pose described by position and orientation.
Rigidly attached coordinate frame; any frame may serve as reference.
notes: Coordinate axes shown on robot base, tool, cube and cylinder. No printed slide number visible in lower-right; physical page27 must not be copied to printedSlideNumber.

title: Kinematics of Manipulators
observedConcepts: Kinematics studies motion without causative forces.
Position, velocity, acceleration, higher derivatives; geometric and time-based properties.
Nearly rigid links connected by joints permitting relative motion.
notes: All text readable; no figure.

title: Joint measurements
observedConcepts: Position sensors measure relative positions of neighboring links.
Revolute/rotary displacement is joint angle; prismatic/sliding displacement is translation/joint offset.
notes: Figure shows base and tool XYZ frames with θ1/θ2/θ3 rotary joints; no prismatic joint is depicted.

title: Forward Kinematics of Manipulators
observedConcepts: Given joint angles compute tool-frame position and orientation relative to base.
notes: Base/tool frame illustration; orientation must not be omitted from forward-kinematics answer.

title: Inverse Kinematics of Manipulators
observedConcepts: Given end-effector position and orientation compute possible joint-angle sets.
Nonlinear equations may lack easy/closed-form solution.
Existence and multiplicity; workspace and unattainable desired pose.
notes: Figure uses tool/base frames. No closed-form method does not itself establish no feasible IK solution; distinguish mathematical solve difficulty from reachability.

title: Jacobian of Manipulator
observedConcepts: Joint rates map to Cartesian velocity by base-frame v = base-frame J(Theta) Theta-dot.
Joint torques from base-frame force/moment vector by tau = J-transpose F.
Singularities: mapping not invertible as described; relevant to users/designers.
notes: Equations visible in upper right. Force vector and Jacobian use matching frame. Figure labels angular velocity omega and linear v; avoid confusing transpose force map with inverse velocity map.

title: Dynamics
observedConcepts: desired trajectory yields actuator torque functions
spatial/temporal path, link/payload mass and joint friction influence torque.
notes: Three distinct torque dependencies visible; no hidden numerical example.
